tools.name: export_web_scripts
tools.title: Export Web Scripts
tools.description: Export JavaScript bytes already retained in one local inspect_web_page or capture_browser_scenario JSON capture (normalized result or complete Evidence). Writes scripts and a digest-verified manifest into an absent absolute output_directory. Returns all source URLs, script or transaction/event references, unavailable states, and an analysis_input for analyze_javascript_application when any bytes were exported. Include script sources in inspect_web_page or select capture.network.response_body in scenarios. No refetch or execution. Safe unambiguous URL layouts preserve relative module paths; versions, query variants, inline scripts, and path collisions are isolated with explicit resolution limitations.

output_directory.description: Absolute absent filesystem directory for verified scripts and manifest; parent directory must exist

If no origin filter is supplied, capture is scoped to the target's current origin. Returns DOM structure, accessibility, scripts, resources, attach-window network and console metadata, workers, and redacted storage inventory as Evidence.

tools.name: compare_web_captures
tools.title: Compare Web Captures
tools.description: Compare passive web captures by providing before and after, each with the complete inspect_web_page normalized_result in inspection and an optional complete discover_webmcp_tools normalized_result in webmcp; or compare recorded scenarios by passing complete capture_browser_scenario normalized_result objects in before_scenario and after_scenario with an optional normalization policy. Use exactly one input group. Network comparison includes observed HTTP requests and WebSocket frame streams; same-URL connections are compared as an unordered collection of ordered streams, retaining connection counts without claiming stable identity between individual connections. Scenario comparison aligns exact step IDs, records deterministic literal normalization, and returns every artifact-level difference plus alignment failures inline. Missing or truncated evidence never proves equality.

after.description: The later or right-hand observation to compare.

tools.name: capture_browser_scenario
tools.title: Capture Browser Scenario
tools.description: Run a controlled browser scenario when passive observation cannot exercise the application. Launch the selected executable or connect to a loopback CDP target, provide a start URL and actions, and select storage or artifacts when needed. Environment, empty storage, and a URL-only final capture are defaults. capture.network selects request_body, response_body, and header_values independently; selected content is returned inline with transaction and event references, byte digests, and explicit unavailable states. Credentials and declared secrets are redacted. Agents can run their own local fixture servers to control application responses. Actions run until completion or cancellation unless timeout_ms is set. Results are returned inline.

browser.description: Required launch/connect selection. Launch uses the selected executable and an owned temporary profile; connect uses one loopback CDP endpoint and target.

start_url.description: Required initial HTTP(S) URL. Query values must be declared separately as public literals or secret references.

environment.description: Optional deterministic browser settings. Defaults to 1280x720, en-US, UTC, light mode, reduced motion, and blocked service workers.

actions.description: Required sequence of explicit browser actions.

storage.description: Optional initial cookies, local storage, or session storage. Defaults to empty; every supplied value and origin must be declared and within the allowed origins.

secrets.description: Optional environment-variable references for values used in actions, URLs, storage, or replay, and for redacting matching observed text. Secret values are never supplied inline.

capture.description: Optional retained artifacts and event families. Defaults to only a final sanitized URL; request screenshots, DOM, accessibility, history, storage, and event capture explicitly.
